single_hypothesis: Making the backward attribute a compile-time template argument (4 kernel objects instead of 2) removes the unused direction's Init/Process code from every object, reducing fixed Scalar overhead on small-workload points without touching DMA, events, or numerics.
changed_mechanism: tiling_key_mhc_expand.h: ASCENDC_TPL_BOOL_DECL(IS_BACKWARD, 0, 1) added; each dtype SEL entry expands over both bool values (sparse_lightning-style multi-value BOOL_SEL), verified by spike to generate 4 kernels with keys 1/257/27/283
op_host: ASCENDC_TPL_SEL_PARAM(context, DT_X, IS_BACKWARD) passes the backward attr into the tiling key; tiling struct and all host tiling policy unchanged (40-byte ABI kept)

op_kernel: entry and class take <DT_X, int IS_BACKWARD> (official built-in convention passes BOOL as int); all runtime backward_ branches become if constexpr on kBackward_; kernel no longer loads tiling.backward

IMPORTANT lesson: compile_cann85.sh resolves the project as <script_dir>/../B_easy, so a scratch project must sit at <parent>/B_easy with the script inside <parent>/<any subdir>; otherwise the ORIGINAL B_easy is silently compiled and the spike proves nothing.

build.notes: Forward kernel text halves (5112 -> 2480); backward drops ~32%. Per-kernel sizes from nm -S.

validation.actual_kernel: 5 CA-simulator cases (fp16/bf16 x fwd/bwd small + fp16 bwd m8), each dispatched to its direction-specific kernel via the correct tiling-key suffix in the config; all executed cleanly (no tiling-size or load errors)
validation.equivalence_audit: Pure dead-code elimination: per direction the executed instruction sequence is the same as the parent's taken branch, minus the runtime direction test, the tiling.backward load, and the input/output length ternary selects. No DMA parameter, event, or arithmetic change.

simulator.interpretation: Unlike rejected E3, every direction improves: forward -6.0% (E3 was +9.3%), backward -2.7~-3.0%. Instruction-count deltas are modest; expected platform effect is likely near the measured noise band (+-1.2), so the submission primarily validates direction and builds the 4-object infrastructure for E5.
